text: PacifiCorp and the project team further defined the grid services through a series of grid services workshops. The workshop meetings have covered the expected event response time, the duration of the event, types of DERs most pertinent to each grid service, any telemetry and control signal requirements, and event notification requirements. Once the DERMS solution was installed and configured in the EMS test environment, PacifiCorp employees worked with OSI to understand the DER configuration requirements that are specific to OSI, which data elements are required and optional within the tool, and the implications of device and group definition. This allowed PacifiCorp to complete the configuration of an existing battery energy storage system (BESS) in the test DERMS solution and pass data between the battery energy management system and the DERMS. Through this testing, PacifiCorp was able to identify that the UDERMS iCommunity project required the latest version release of the OSI DERMS software. This step marked the validation that the OSI Monarch and Integra DERMS solution could be effectively utilized in an EMS test environment and kicked off additional IT steps needed to have dedicated hardware and environments that are needed for the UDERMS project. As part of the deployment of the dedicated sandbox implementation of the DERMS, PacifiCorp completed detailed discussion on cybersecurity, IT hardware specifications, base software and system requirements, networking, physical installation requirements, access requirements, and operator requirements. There was a need for detailed IT system architecture discussions including security configuration and system/network analysis due to 7 the nature of integrations that are required from the OSI Integra DERMS in the EMS sandbox environment to externally located systems and devices. The core IT solution design discussions were completed between June and October of 2023 and equipment procurement and delivery was completed between November and December 2023. At the end of December 2023, all required IT equipment was received by PacifiCorp for deployment of the OSI software in the dedicated PacifiCorp sandbox environment. In parallel, system installation of the dedicated OSI Monarch and Integra DERMS solutions started on a virtual machine hosted by OSI and migration and configuration of that software package was planned for when the final server in the PacifiCorp environment was available. Throughout the period of system and environment design and procurement processes, the PacifiCorp and OSI teams met on several occasions to conduct several DER workbook training sessions to understand the software licensing implications on the DER configuration and execution within the DERMS. A series of workshop sessions were completed to discuss the detailed data elements outlined in the OSI DER workbook and how the project solution architecture intersects with the software configuration capabilities.
